title: Rc Signing Audit
objective: Audit macOS and Windows signing/notarization plus publication/rollback, producing an exact human credential-gated checklist without using credentials.

runs.command: bash -lc bash -n scripts/release-macos.sh && pnpm test:release && git diff --check

handoff.summary: Audited the implemented macOS Developer ID/notarytool and Windows Authenticode/Azure Artifact Signing paths, plus the tagged GitHub and npm publication workflow. DISTRIBUTION.md now separates credential-free evidence, credential-gated automation, manual clean-machine acceptance, and unproved production signing; provides exact unsigned verification, macOS hardened-runtime/notarization/stapling, one-way publication, website, rollback, revocation, and secret-hygiene checklists. WINDOWS.md now gives an exact PFX/Azure verification and SmartScreen acceptance procedure. No credentials were accessed and no signature or notarization result is claimed.
risks: No production Apple, Azure/PFX, npm, or GitHub credentialed tag was exercised, so the final signing and publication chain remains an evidence gate.
The tag workflow does not yet name a protected GitHub release Environment and its external actions use version tags rather than immutable commit SHAs.
The audited base archives have adjacent checksums but no consolidated release manifest; the parallel manifest lane may make that statement stale during integration.

The current macOS PKG installs only the executables under /usr/local/bin, has manual removal, and only the PKG can carry a stapled ticket; Windows SmartScreen reputation remains external to Authenticode.

pnpm test:portable was attempted after a standard build but failed in the isolated lane because current FLINT headers and addons were not installed; 265 of 271 tests passed and all six failures required that absent native prefix.
next_steps: Reconcile the release-manifest wording after the rc-manifest lane lands.
Protect v* tags, add a maintainer-approved release Environment, and review or pin secret-bearing GitHub Actions before the first production tag.
Run the full portable, native, and SEA suites from the integrated release-candidate workspace where the native stack is already installed.
Perform a credentialed dry run without publication, then execute Gatekeeper and SmartScreen checks on ordinary clean target machines.
After all evidence is approved, publish from one annotated tag and test the public GitHub, npm, installer, Jupyter, and website paths in that order.
